title: Triterpenoid saponins from Ilex latifolia inhibit breast cancer growth by disrupting the SREBP1/FASN-mediated lipid metabolic pathway.
authors: Wang, Fangfang; Wang, Mingjie; Shi, Zihan; Wu, Yongchen; Wang, Cunqin; Wang, Hongting
one_liner_zh: 研究三萜皂苷抑制乳腺癌脂代谢通路，分子对接仅涉及小分子与蛋白SREBP-1，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Dysregulated lipid metabolism is a hallmark of breast cancer progression, with the SREBP-1/FASN axis serving as a key driver of tumor growth and survival. Natural products offer a valuable reservoir of metabolic modulators, yet their mechanisms and translational potential remain insufficiently defined. Here, we investigated the anti-breast cancer effects of Kundinoside D (KD-D), a triterpenoid saponin isolated from Ilex latifolia, and evaluated the in vivo efficacy of its bioactive extract fractions. In vitro, KD-D suppressed proliferation, induced apoptosis, and caused G1/G2 cell-cycle arrest in luminal (MCF-7) and triple-negative (MDA-MB-231) breast cancer cells. KD-D markedly downregulated SREBP-1 and FASN expression, as confirmed by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Functional assays using siRNA-mediated knockdown and pharmacological inhibition of SREBP-1 enhanced KD-D-induced apoptosis, validating the functional significance of this pathway. Molecular docking predicted stable binding of KD-D to SREBP-1, which was experimentally supported by a cellular thermal shift assay demonstrating direct protein stabilization. Rescue experiments further showed that overexpression of constitutively active nuclear SREBP-1 partially restored cell viability and triglyceride synthesis following KD-D treatment. In vivo, oral administration of Ilex latifolia n-butanol and ethyl acetate fractions significantly suppressed MCF-7 xenograft growth, induced tumor necrosis, and reduced SREBP-1/FASN expression without causing weight loss. Collectively, these findings identify SREBP-1 as a direct molecular target of KD-D and demonstrate that Ilex latifolia-derived constituents exert potent antitumor effects through lipid metabolism inhibition, underscoring their potential as metabolism-targeted therapeutics for breast cancer.
abstract_zh: 脂质代谢失调是乳腺癌进展的一个标志，其中SREBP-1/FASN轴作为肿瘤生长和存活的关键驱动因素。天然产物提供了代谢调节剂的宝贵资源，但其机制和转化潜力仍未得到充分阐明。在此，我们研究了从大叶冬青（Ilex latifolia）中分离的三萜皂苷Kundinoside D（KD-D）的抗乳腺癌作用，并评估了其生物活性提取物组分的体内疗效。在体外，KD-D抑制腔面型（MCF-7）和三阴性（MDA-MB-231）乳腺癌细胞的增殖，诱导凋亡，并引起G1/G2细胞周期阻滞。通过Western blotting和免疫荧光证实，KD-D显著下调SREBP-1和FASN表达。使用siRNA介导的敲低和SREBP-1药理学抑制的功能实验增强了KD-D诱导的凋亡，验证了该通路的功能重要性。分子对接预测KD-D与SREBP-1稳定结合，并通过细胞热位移实验证实其直接稳定蛋白，从而在实验上支持了这一预测。拯救实验进一步表明，组成性激活的核SREBP-1过表达部分恢复了KD-D处理后的细胞活力和甘油三酯合成。在体内，口服大叶冬青正丁醇和乙酸乙酯组分显著抑制MCF-7异种移植瘤生长，诱导肿瘤坏死，并降低SREBP-1/FASN表达，且未引起体重减轻。综合这些发现，确定SREBP-1为KD-D的直接分子靶点，并证明大叶冬青来源成分通过脂质代谢抑制发挥强效抗肿瘤作用，凸显了其作为乳腺癌代谢靶向治疗药物的潜力。
